full_form: Adrenal tumour -> Neuroblastoma, NOS (9500) or Pheochromocytoma, NOS (8700)
notes: A referral description, not a diagnosis. Both neuroblastoma and pheochromocytoma arise in the adrenal medulla. Age, the catecholamine profile and the immunohistochemistry separate them: urinary vanillylmandelic acid and homovanillic acid point to 9500 Neuroblastoma, NOS; plasma free metanephrines or 24-hour urinary fractionated metanephrines point to 8700 Pheochromocytoma, NOS. PHOX2B is positive in both and separates neither; GATA3 and S100/SOX10-positive sustentacular cells in a zellballen pattern are what separate them. An adrenal cortical tumour is not in this group at all.

notes: 9490 Ganglioneuroblastoma. The intermediate step of the neuroblastic spectrum: Schwannian stroma-rich tissue containing ganglion cells. The distinction from neuroblastoma is histological and needs the pathology report, not the referral wording.

9490 Ganglioneuroblastoma. The International Neuroblastoma Pathology Committee category for Schwannian stroma-rich tissue with ganglion cells intermixed throughout and no separate nodule. The subtype is recorded alongside the code; it does not change the number.

notes: 9490 Ganglioneuroblastoma. The International Neuroblastoma Pathology Committee category for one or more distinct neuroblastic nodules inside a ganglioneuroma or intermixed background. A nodule within a ganglioneuroma is this entity, not a ganglioneuroma.
coding_note: INPC categories per Shimada 1999, reproduced as Table 1 of Mete O, et al., Endocr Pathol 2022;33(1):90-114, p. 108 (contract Sec.10.1).

full_form: Ganglioneuroma -> benign; no ICCC-3 Group IV code is assigned
notes: A fully matured ganglioneuroma is benign. ICD-O-3.2 codes it 9490 Ganglioneuroma at behaviour /0, and ICCC-3 Group IV registers behaviour /3 only, so no Group IV code is assigned and the case is referred to the registrar. Do not reach for 9490 Ganglioneuroblastoma, which is the malignant tumour on the same four-digit stem. Read the report before deciding: a specimen containing ganglioneuroma tissue is a ganglioneuroma only if the report states there is no neuroblastic component anywhere and no separate paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma component. A neuroblastic nodule inside it is 9490 Ganglioneuroblastoma, nodular, and a pheochromocytoma component makes it a composite tumour.

No alias target is carried here: listing 9490 would make 'Ganglioneuroma' display as a synonym of 9490/3 Ganglioneuroblastoma, which is the exact trap D1 exists to close. The tree states the exclusion on the histology step, which carries the six-key exclusion object naming 9490/0 Ganglioneuroma. This overrides alias-instruction entry 6, which mapped the string to 9490.

Use this code when the report says parasympathetic but names no site; a named site gives a more specific code - carotid body is 8692 Carotid body paraganglioma and middle ear or jugulotympanic is 8690 Middle ear paraganglioma.

notes: This is not a Group IV tumour. ICD-O-3.2 moved Ewing sarcoma onto 9364 and made it the code for peripheral neuroectodermal tumour at the same time, so this wording is 9364 Ewing sarcoma. Code the case from the ICCC-3 Group VIII tree (bone tumours) at a bony primary and from the Group IX tree (soft tissue sarcomas) at a soft-tissue primary. The site is the only question left to answer. Note the difference from the unqualified wording: primitive neuroectodermal tumour, NOS and PNET, NOS without 'peripheral' are 9473 CNS embryonal tumor, NOS, which is ICCC-3 Group III.

Overrides alias-instruction entries 30, 31 and 33, which sent this wording to 9503. icdo32.sqlite, checked against both the 2019 draft and the 9 Oct 2020 final: 9364/3 Preferred 'Ewing sarcoma'; Synonym 'Ewing tumor', 'Peripheral neuroectodermal tumor', 'PPNET'; Related 'Peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor', 'Neuroectodermal tumor, NOS'. IARC, 3.1 to 3.2 Summary of main changes, Ewing sarcoma: 'Ewing sarcoma (9260/3) has moved to, and is now the preferred term for, 9364/3 (peripheral neuroectodermal tumour).' No Group IV morphology target is carried, because 9364 is not a Group IV code (rule 8) and the case leaves the group; the destination is named in the referral fields instead, which is D4's design. nci_concept_id is null - the concept the alias instructions pre-recorded, NCIT:C3716, is the CNS 'Primitive Neuroectodermal Tumor', not the Ewing family.

notes: This wording is not a defined pathology term and the tool does not read it as one. What happens next is decided by the immunohistochemistry already in the file, not by the words in the report. CD99 positive with PHOX2B negative and synaptophysin negative is an Ewing-family tumour, which is coded from the bone group at a bony primary and the soft tissue group at a soft-tissue primary. Anything else, or a panel that was not done, is 9503 Neuroepithelioma, NOS, with CD99, PHOX2B and synaptophysin recorded as outstanding work-up. Do not order new testing to answer this - answer from what is already in the file.
coding_note: RULING D6 (contract Sec.6). The exact phrase 'peripheral neuroepithelioma' appears NOWHERE in ICD-O-3.2 - not as a term, a synonym, a see-also, an inclusion or an exclusion. Verified by full-text query of icdo32.sqlite across term, see_also, includes, excludes and other_text on 18 Sep 2026; the only 'neuroepithelioma' strings in the workbook are 9503/3 Neuroepithelioma, NOS, 9523/3 Olfactory neuroepithelioma and its synonym Esthesioneuroepithelioma, and the level-2 heading Neuroepitheliomatous neoplasms. Layer 1 is silent, so 9503 is the only plausible home and nothing in Layer 1 says so. Entry node is the CD99 step rather than the tree's own first step, as D6 directs; the word 'peripheral' already excludes the C70.0-C72.9 range that the first step gates on, so no dual-group check is skipped by entering there.

notes: Standard clinical abbreviation for paraganglioma: 8680 Paraganglioma, NOS until the site is documented.
The British spelling of pheochromocytoma: 8700 Pheochromocytoma, NOS. Common in pathology reports wherever medical training follows British conventions.
Ward shorthand for pheochromocytoma: 8700 Pheochromocytoma, NOS.
8700 Pheochromocytoma, NOS. An old name implying a malignant pheochromocytoma; ICD-O-3.2 carries it on the same code, which has one behaviour only.

origin_system: WHO Classification of Endocrine and Neuroendocrine Tumours 2022
notes: 8700 Pheochromocytoma, NOS - a catecholamine-producing tumour of the adrenal medulla. Diagnosis rests on plasma free metanephrines or 24-hour urinary fractionated metanephrines with imaging. ICD-O-3.2 carries 8700 at behaviour /3 only: there is no benign and no malignant pheochromocytoma code to choose between.

The ICD-O-3.2 preferred term on 8700 at behaviour /3, and the only term the tool records on this code. The ICD-O-3.1 strings 'Pheochromocytoma, malignant' and 'Pheochromocytoma, benign' no longer exist.
coding_note: Contract Sec.0.4 and Sec.10.1b. IARC's Deleted codes and their terms records 8700/0 deleted and the /1 terms moved to /3 across 868-870; WHO abolished the benign and malignant adjectives in the 4th edition, 2017 (Mete 2022, p. 100). ICD-O behaviour /3 is 'malignant, primary site', not a prognosis - a low observed metastatic rate is not an argument for a lower behaviour.

full_form: Pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma -> Pheochromocytoma, NOS (8700) or Paraganglioma, NOS (8680)
notes: The abbreviation the WHO literature uses for the pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma family as a whole. It names a family, not a diagnosis: an adrenal medullary primary is 8700 Pheochromocytoma, NOS, and an extra-adrenal primary takes a paraganglioma code chosen by site, falling back to 8680 Paraganglioma, NOS.
coding_note: No NCIt concept was queried for the family abbreviation; the two entity concepts are carried on the Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma entries. Abbreviation in general use throughout Mete O, et al., Endocr Pathol 2022;33(1):90-114.

notes: 9504 Spongioneuroblastoma. A 1948 term with no modern diagnostic criteria and no current WHO entity behind it. No step of this group's decision trees leads to it. It is kept so that an older record already carrying the code can be found and read; do not assign it to a new case - take the diagnosis to the registrar instead. Topography decides the group: 9501 to 9504 belong to ICCC-3 Group III everywhere in C70.0 to C72.9 - meninges, brain and spinal cord - and to Group IV only outside that range. Record the topography before anything else.
coding_note: RULING D2 (contract Sec.2.3, Sec.6, Sec.8 rule 4). icdo32.sqlite prints 'Spongioneuroblastoma' on 9504/3 as a plain Preferred term with no [obs] marker, so the Group 3 [obs] test does not remove it; it is retained in this group's code list and flagged, and reachable from no tree. This entry is the alias D2 provides for, so it deliberately carries no tree and no entry step - it resolves the code and nothing else. Group 3's alias file carries the same string against 9504 for the C70.0-C72.9 range.

notes: 8681 Sympathetic paraganglioma - a paraganglioma of the sympathetic chain, typically retroperitoneal, paraspinal or posterior mediastinal, and usually catecholamine-producing. Where the site is extra-adrenal but the report does not say which paraganglion, use 8693 Extra-adrenal paraganglioma, NOS.
coding_note: NCIt C4216 also lists 'Chromaffin tumor' and 'Chromaffinoma' as synonyms of sympathetic paraganglioma. ICD-O-3.2 carries both strings on 8700/3 instead, so they are aliased there and are deliberately kept out of this entry's synonym list (ruling D5 - Layer 1 governs term placement).

notes: 9502 Teratoid medulloepithelioma, NOS at a peripheral, non-central-nervous-system site - a medulloepithelioma containing heterologous elements such as cartilage, muscle or bone. Topography decides the group: 9501 to 9504 belong to ICCC-3 Group III everywhere in C70.0 to C72.9 - meninges, brain and spinal cord - and to Group IV only outside that range.
